Proof in the paper: Figure 2 shows that the β-PdZn alloy has formed by reduction using XRD. The alloy has shifted diffraction peaks at 41.2° and ∼44° compared with monometallic Pd at ∼40°. Further, energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping in a scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) (Figure 3 and Figure S2) quite clearly shows the formation of the alloy on catalyst 1, whereas prior to reduction, STEM-EDX shows that the catalyst comprises of PdO particles on ZnO (Figure S3). Using HAADF STEM, the lattice can be resolved, Figure 4 and Figure S2, and is the same as that reported by Nowicka et al., who obtained atomic resolution images of the lattice showing the good order in the particle lattice; (26) the lattice projection of the [0–10] plane is shown in the figure.
